title: Mitigate per-customer latency skew from concurrent warmups across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Priya Narang
description: Multiple customers reported 2–8s increases in time-to-first-token (TTFT) and drop in tokens/sec after a regional incident on 2026-03-11. Root cause triage indicates a race between concurrent warmup priming, KV cache prefetches, and eviction heuristics across hosted/dedicated/private runtimes. When many sessions begin simultaneously, warmup prefetch floods router/scheduler leading to per-customer tail latency spikes and throughput oscillation. This ticket scopes an urgent production hotfix: introduce coordinated warmup admission, per-tenant warmup rate limits, prefetch batching window, and a short-term eviction backoff to stabilize TTFT while we build longer-term scheduler-level fairness and telemetry.
acceptance_criteria: TTFT median for affected customers returns to baseline (+/-10%) under multi-tenant warmup surge
Tokens/sec (aggregate) recovers to prior baseline and per-customer variance reduced by >60%
No elevated error rates or OOMs introduced by patch during 2-hour canary in us-east-1
Canary rollout and rollback automation documented in PR and console runbook
work_items: Add warmup admission controller: global token-bucket per-region + per-customer sub-buckets (engine change)
Throttle prefetch window: introduce 50ms batching window for KV prefetch requests
Eviction backoff patch: when admission detects surge, temporarily raise eviction thresholds for 30s
Instrumentation: add per-tenant warmup counters, prefetch queue depth, kernel-selection fallback metric
Canary plan: us-east-1 3 hosts -> 10 hosts -> region-wide with automated smoke checks
Postmortem & follow-up: scheduler fairness RFC and long-term mitigations

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Admission controller misconfiguration could over-throttle legitimate bursty workloads -> Mitigation: conservative default rates + feature flag + per-tenant override
Risk: Prefetch batching increases memory pressure -> Mitigation: cap batch size, monitor mem usage, adjust window dynamically
Risk: Eviction backoff may delay convergence for long contexts -> Mitigation: time-limited backoff (30s) and metric alerts for abnormal cache growth
Risk: Cross-deployment behavior differences (private clusters with older runtime) -> Mitigation: ship compatibility shim and documented upgrade notes
qa_and_rollout_notes: Canary smoke checks: realtime TTFT, tokens/sec, queue depths, kernel-fallback-count, OOM rate
Automated rollback triggers: >20% error increase OR TTFT worse than baseline for 10m
Private customers: patch available as runtime-1.21-hotfix-20260315; sched teams to coordinate maintenance windows
